assessment_goal: Identify the core definition of computer science as the study of algorithms and computation, distinguishing it from merely the study of hardware or software engineering.
misconception_target: Confusing computer science with computer engineering or IT support, focusing on physical components rather than abstract problem-solving.

assessment_goal: Recall the role of binary representation as the fundamental data format for all digital information processing in computer systems.
misconception_target: Believing that computers process information directly in decimal or text formats without conversion to binary.

assessment_goal: Define the concept of an algorithm as a finite, well-defined sequence of steps for solving a problem.
misconception_target: Viewing an algorithm as a specific piece of code or a programming language syntax rather than an abstract procedure.

assessment_goal: Identify the significance of mathematical notation and set theory in formally describing computational structures and data relationships.
misconception_target: Assuming that theoretical foundations are purely abstract and have no practical application in defining data structures or system logic.

assessment_goal: Recognize the standard pedagogical structure of a lecture, specifically the 'Introduce' phase, which sets the context and learning objectives before detailed content delivery.
misconception_target: Believing that the introduction phase is optional or that lectures should begin immediately with complex technical details without framing.
